questions.q: How does the summary describe the unconscious mind?
a: As the fastest information filter in the world
As a slow but highly accurate analyst
As a storehouse of forgotten memories
As a purely emotional decision maker
questions.why: It sifts new information instantly and presents a judgment based on the few big factors.

questions.q: Why can over-analyzing an apartment choice lead to a worse decision?
a: Minor details crowd out the few factors that matter
The decision becomes too emotional to judge
You start comparing it with unrelated purchases
You lose the ability to picture the rooms
questions.why: The summary says small puzzle pieces can hide the much more important ones.

questions.q: What happens to your judgment under intense stress?
a: Face reading declines and you develop tunnel vision
You become faster and more accurate at reading people
You rely more on past experience and less on threats
You stop noticing physical danger altogether
questions.why: Stress narrows attention to the most imminent threat, which leads the gut astray.

questions.q: What should you do in a stressful moment to protect your judgment?
a: Reduce the stress quickly by walking or breathing
Make the decision immediately before doubts grow
Collect as much extra data as possible
Ask someone else to decide for you
questions.why: The summary suggests cooling off or continuing the conversation later.

questions.q: Why do the judges on The Voice face away from the singers?
a: So only the voice influences their choice
So the audience cannot see their reactions
So singers cannot tailor their performance
So the show can reveal them dramatically
questions.why: The chairs act as a screen that keeps appearance from biasing the judges.
